_comment: Walk-on structures that aren't native terrain -- bridges, docks, wooden platforms, stone floors (see include/Structures.h). Each is placed as ONE resizable LDtk entity whose identifier is the key here; the importer tiles this 9-slice art across the entity's rect and tags it surface=<surface> (so visuals, collision, footsteps fall out of the one placed box -- no per-tile painting). Cells are [col,row] in the 16px SOURCE tileset (importer x2's to the 32px world atlas). Positions: nw/n/ne = top edge, w/c/e = middle, sw/s/se = bottom edge; a thin structure uses only the relevant caps/column (linear bridge = the 1-wide sub-case). 'walkable' is per-slice: a slice's art always renders, but only walkable=true slices become footing (walkable + surface); walkable=false slices are cosmetic OVERHANG (e.g. a bridge's side rails hang over water -- rendered, but you don't walk there, and the underlying terrain's walkability is left untouched). Default true if omitted. 'surface' is the LDtk Surface enum value. Add a type (Dock, etc.) by adding an entry + a matching LDtk entity.
